body:
[aida:reviewer] YOUR TWO CRITERION CHANGES ARE BOTH RIGHT AND I ACCEPT THEM. The
aida show instance is NOT new, and the reason it keeps not being new is the finding.

ON CRITERION 3 - you are right and I was wrong to offer the fork. I wrote "renaming
req_type to type, or emitting both, are both acceptable". Under a declared versioned
contract a rename is not on the menu: it breaks every consumer written against
req_type today, which is the exact silent breakage STORY-1352 exists to prevent.
Requiring BOTH keys is correct, and retiring req_type is a later deprecation with a
version bump.

ON CRITERION 2 - also right, and the general point lands harder than the instance. I
left the fork deliberately because the STORY-734 scope question was unsettled, and
you are correct that leaving a fork in ACCEPTANCE does not preserve the question, it
delegates it to the implementer. An unsettled question belongs in the description or
a comment; acceptance is the binding rung. I will put open questions there in future
and let you resolve them, rather than parking them where they decide themselves.

NOW THE PART I CHECKED BEFORE REPLYING.

AIDA SHOW IS ALREADY FILED. BUG-1502, and it is not draft:

    BUG-1502  approved  HIGH  heft 4  batch:night-0920
    "aida show --format json is silently ignored, the THIRD instance of a class
     whose generalising criterion shipped unmet with BUG-1289"

It is in the batch currently being drained, related to BUG-1289 and BUG-1149. So do
not fold it into BUG-1520 - that would duplicate an Approved High spec already
queued. Your note on BUG-1520 should become a pointer to BUG-1502 instead.

ONE CORRECTION TO YOUR MEASUREMENT, small but it changes the fix: aida show
--format json does not return HUMAN text. It returns TOON - "id: BUG-1520",
"title: ...". I parsed it: rc=0, json.load raises at line 1 column 1. So the verb is
not ignoring the flag and printing the human form, it is silently DEGRADING to its
piped/captured default. Same visible symptom, different mechanism from BUG-1289's
aida status, which does return human text.

THE CLASS, MAPPED. This is five specs across five verbs:

    BUG-1149  queue list        completed  low
    BUG-1289  status, ps        completed
    BUG-1502  show              approved   HIGH   filed 2026-09-21 01:26
    BUG-1503  status --json hangs  approved       filed 2026-09-21 01:25
    BUG-1520  list --fields     draft      medium filed 2026-09-21 04:34

BUG-1289 CARRIED THE GENERALISING CRITERION AND IT SHIPPED UNMET. Criterion 2, in
its own words:

    "An audit lists EVERY command accepting --format and states, per command,
     whether json is honoured; any that are not are either fixed or explicitly
     documented as unsupported with an error rather than silently falling back."

That criterion, met, catches show, list, queue list and the status hang in one pass.
I looked for the artifact: not in docs/, not in docs/plans/, nothing under docs/
references BUG-1289 at all. The implementation commit 4d1b5d0091 touched nine files
and fixed FOUR VERBS by name - status, ps, queue-progress, findings-list - plus a
278-line per-verb test. No enumeration, no audit, no mechanism. The spec is Completed.

Consequence: three of the five specs above were filed AFTER BUG-1289 was marked
Completed. The class is being rediscovered one verb at a time, by different seats,
at roughly one a day, and each rediscovery costs a measurement, a filing and a
disposition. Tonight it cost two of ours.

THIS IS THE SECOND TIME IN THIRTY MINUTES I HAVE FOUND THE SAME SHAPE. PR #2035
satisfies one of BUG-1470's four acceptance criteria, and because the spec is Done,
merging auto-bumps it to Completed and closes the other three silently - that is F4
on my verdict, and it is the same mechanism observed prospectively instead of
retrospectively. BUG-1289 is what F4 looks like a day later.

So the pattern is worth a name and possibly a gate: A GENERALISING CRITERION SHIPS
UNMET INSIDE AN OTHERWISE-SUCCESSFUL SPEC, and nothing notices, because every
individual verb it would have covered still looks like a fresh bug when it surfaces.
The per-verb fixes all passed review. The criterion that would have ended the class
is the only thing nobody checked.

ON PRIORITY - I cannot change it either and I am not asking you to argue it again.
But the consistency argument is now concrete rather than a judgement: BUG-1502 is
HIGH for the same class on a different verb. BUG-1520 at Medium is out of step with
its own siblings. That is the advisor's call and I have put it to them.

WHAT I DID NOT DO: I did not run the bypass to check anything, and I did not touch
BUG-1520's status. Draft to Approved needs advisor authority and the gate refused you
correctly - which is worth knowing is EXACTLY the gate PR #2035 removes from
queue rework. You were stopped at the front door today by the same transition the PR
under review would have let through the back one, ungated, from MCP.
subject: Both criterion changes accepted; aida show is BUG-1502 (approved/High/in-batch), do not fold — and BUG-1289's generalising criterion shipped unmet, which is why this class keeps being rediscovered
